items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I did some gigs with different musicians and later wne into the "Reve" a dance hall in the Rex theater building with Charlie "Dizzy" Lewis who had also engaged George Johnson on alto-sax.

ctx.x: It was at this point that I decided that I would go back to Europe. I felt that I would have a better chance to make a living, and I'd always been in love with the European atmosphere. You could go where you wanted to go, and spend your money where you liked. There wasn't the prejudice that you had in the States, and it was my idea of living. I decided I was going to stay. I felt that if I came to Europe I would probably be getting a second chance at life. I wasn't down on the thought that nothing in New York was…

One letter I received from Charles that had no date, mentioned that he almost had a contract for me to play with Charlie "Dizzy" Lewis and "Big Boy" Goudie but he didn't mention where. The next one was dated the 7th of October and mentioned that he was on the verge of getting me a contract in a new club that was going to open and asked me if I was still interested. I wrote immediately and told him, I was and also would agree to the conditions which were not bad.

At the time, I was rehearsing with a group of musicians of whom I can only remember one musician who was Austin "Slim" Moore, a trombonist. I had known "Slim" a long time. He was about 6 feet 4 and weighed 190 or perhaps 200 pounds, and was a long way from actually being slim. The pianist-and leader was a pianist who lived on 135th street between a couple of times a week and we had done a couple of gigs together. Most of the cats were beginning to dig the modern jive and I remember the first one of those numbers…
